_note: The parameter catalogue for this corpus: every number a statute did not state, with its unit (the corpus's own units are accepted and scaled by the decoder), the convention its value comes from and its source. It starts empty: the plan decides which parameters exist and proposes each with a provisional value, and the harness enters the proposal here marked `proposed` (run, iteration, node) until the operator reviews it by removing the marker or changing the value; the doctor lists every unreviewed proposal. The operator-authored list this file carried before any law was planned is kept, out of the pipeline's path, under readings/legacy/. Figures the law states are literals on the rule's span, never entries here.

params.name: p.reversal_window
params.convention: the manoeuvre-recognition window of a turning study: the longest a passenger vehicle takes to carry a direction reversal through, from the first steering input to the heading it ends with, at the speeds such a turn is made at
params.source: turning-path and low-speed manoeuvre timings in highway geometric design practice (AASHTO Green Book design-vehicle turning paths)

params.name: p.reversal_heading_tolerance
params.convention: the band about a half turn within which an accumulated heading change counts as a reversal rather than a single turn or a full circle: half the angle between a quarter turn and a half turn, so that a right-angle turn falls outside the band and a turn that overshoots or falls short of the opposite heading by a quarter turn still counts
params.source: manoeuvre classification tolerances in vehicle-trajectory annotation practice

params.name: p.curvature_resolution
params.convention: the smallest horizontal curvature a map or perception source resolves above its alignment noise; below it the roadway reads as straight. Stated as the reciprocal of the radius beyond which a rural alignment is treated as tangent
params.source: alignment tolerances in highway geometric design and in map-matching practice

params.name: p.crest_approach_distance
params.convention: the length of the approach to a crest within which a driver is in the zone of restricted sight the crest creates, taken as the stopping sight distance of a rural design speed
params.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, crest vertical curve and stopping sight distance tables

params.name: p.yaw_rate_resolution
params.convention: the smallest rate of change of heading a source resolves above its noise floor; below it the road user reads as not turning
params.source: noise floors of inertial and trajectory-differentiated yaw rate in vehicle instrumentation practice

params.name: p.motion_speed_resolution
params.convention: the smallest speed a trajectory source resolves above its position noise; below it the road user reads as at rest rather than moving
params.source: speed noise floors in vehicle-trajectory and radar instrumentation practice

params.name: p.reaction_time
params.convention: the brake reaction time of the stopping-sight-distance model: the time from the driver's seeing an object in the road to the application of the brakes, during which the vehicle holds its speed
params.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, stopping sight distance

params.name: p.decel_dry
params.convention: the deceleration the stopping-sight-distance model assumes a driver achieves on a dry paved surface within the limits of the tyre-pavement friction available and of the driver's control
params.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, stopping sight distance

params.name: p.decel_wet
params.convention: the same model's deceleration on a wet paved surface, the friction class the design guide applies to wet-pavement braking
params.source: AASHTO wet-pavement friction classes for stopping sight distance

params.name: p.decel_ice
params.convention: the same model's deceleration on an icy or snow-covered surface, the lowest friction class of winter-driving guidance
params.source: winter-surface friction classes in highway maintenance and winter-driving guidance

params.name: p.seeing_distance_darkness
params.convention: the distance ahead a driver can see an unlit object on low-beam headlamps in darkness; it caps the distance clear ahead at night however far the road's own sight distance reaches
params.source: headlamp-reach and night-visibility distances in lighting design practice

params.name: p.narrow_lane_width
params.convention: the lane width below which a design guide treats the lane as narrow and applies a reduction factor; the lower end of its lane-width standards
params.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, lane widths

params.name: p.narrow_lane_margin
params.convention: the factor by which the required clear distance is raised where the lane is below the design width, the narrow-lane adjustment of the design guide's capacity and safety factors
params.source: narrow-lane adjustment factors in highway capacity and design practice

params.name: p.path_lateral_clearance
params.convention: the lateral clearance between the nearest points of two bodies within which a road user ahead stands in the path the subject's body sweeps; beyond it the road user is to one side of that path and is passed rather than followed
params.source: the side clearance of safe-passing standards between a vehicle and the road user it passes, at the lower end of the distances vehicle codes and design guidance state

_fields.aggregates: optional operator overrides only: word, classes (ru.* ids or other words). The run derives every aggregate the laws use from the corpus definitions (results/<run>/reading.json, for review); an operator entry here takes precedence over the derived one.
